items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And they had the entertainers, John Wycliffe had the band of entertainers.

ctx.x: Well, I never did know whether she could have been married then as far as I knew. Yeah. But Joe had several women pianists. It seemed like there was more women pianists who played that type of music than the men. Now there was a pianist up there from here called Arthur Campbell too. He played with George Field in the spot. And later on, fellas like Tom Aladdin came up and Mutt was up there for a while. And they came up, I think Mary Mack, like Mary Mack had, they played at the Monogram Theater. And so they began…
Did you ever see Big Jim Coliseum around?

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Yeah, John Wycliffe had the band entertainers.

ctx.x: It was a company, wasn't it? John Wycliffe.

Yeah, John Wycliffe had the band entertainers. And the Deluxe and the Dreamin' was open. Then you had Jimmy Loom and the Vendome was going big. And Louie was doubling. Later on, before Louie came back, then he doubled from the Vendome. The Vendome to the Sunset. That's when Natty Dominic was playing there with him, you understand? And Dutre. All those bands split up and the men just went like the Four Wings. Dutre was over there with Carol Dixon's band. So I may be in some instances, I may be a little ahead of…
